A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CauScale with matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices (A-D in v1; A-F in v2) are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on synthetic SCM and simulated gene-expression data, including accuracy, runtime, memory usage and ablations (Table 1; Figures 3-7).

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds cyclicity, causal-effect metrics, robustness experiments and observational-only evaluations (Tables 2, 4-7; Figure 7).

M1.justification: The core two-stream design and prediction head remain. v2 introduces iterative removal of the lowest-scoring edge in detected cycles as post-processing for acyclic outputs and AID evaluation (Section 5.3; Appendix F.1). The newly disclosed delay of the first reduction does not establish that the network was redesigned or retrained.

E1.justification: The synthetic SCM and SERGIO-GRN domains remain. v2 adds targeted synthetic scenarios with hidden common causes (Section 5.6) and purely observational inputs (Appendix F.3), extending input conditions without adding a new dataset domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same setting-specific comparator membership: CORR, INVCOV, FCI, NOTEARS, SDCD, DiffAN, AVICI and SEA-GIES. The new AID comparisons use existing baselines; the revised SEA checkpoint description concerns training settings rather than a new comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 adds AID evaluation with cycle-breaking, broader cyclicity assessment, hidden-node removal protocols, restricted prior-estimation sample counts and observational-only testing. Appendix C also replaces the statement that SEA was trained on the authors' data throughout with use of a public checkpoint for synthetic Stage 1. This is a reported protocol revision; rerunning the retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of cycle frequency and removal effects, robustness to hidden high-out-degree nodes, sensitivity to noisy graph priors, and performance without interventions (Section 5.3, Sections 5.6-5.7 and Appendix F.3). Figure 4 also revises graph-component ablation results. Existing pooling, distribution-shift and sample-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports averages over five independent test graphs without standard deviations. v2 systematically adds mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for all main CauScale settings and the AID comparisons (Tables 5-6). The five-graph count is retained; additional training runs or seeds are not established.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises CauScale's SERGIO-GRN mAP from 71.4 to 54.0 at 100 nodes and 34.5 to 39.2 at 200 nodes; corresponding AUC values change from 95.1 to 90.5 and 90.3 to 90.8. Figure 4 changes ablation values, while new tables and Figure 7 add substantial cyclicity, AID, robustness and observational results. The SERGIO-GRN revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: New Appendix E derives forward-pass FLOP costs and supplies Proposition E.1 with a peak-inference-memory proof using m > n. Section 4.6 also revises the predicted sample-axis/node-axis compute fractions from 26.64%/38.75% to 36.60%/48.13%, accounting for the delayed first reduction.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same claims: efficient, accurate amortized discovery, training up to 500 nodes, inference up to 1,000 nodes, headline mAP of 99.6%/84.4%, and 4-13,000-fold speedups. Added evidence and limitations do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of failures under severe confounding, increasing sensitivity to prior quality, cycles under joint size/mechanism shift, and cases where SDCD has lower AID. It also proposes an optimization-based explanation for reduction benefits. The conclusion explicitly acknowledges missing real-world observational validation and generalization limits of simulated training.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly documents first reduction after k+1 blocks. Appendix C identifies SEA's Stage 1 public checkpoint and adds training costs of 48 GPU-hours for synthetic Stage 2 and 72 GPU-hours for SERGIO-GRN. CauScale's hardware, hyperparameters, training schedule and project-access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds Granger/time-series approaches citing Gallagher, Tank, and Brown and Carlson, plus an explicit comparison with SEA's strategy. Henckel et al. is added for AID, and attribution of the decomposed prediction head changes from Lippe et al. to Wu et al. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order remain. Local additions expand related work, explanations and limitations, introduce two robustness subsections and Appendices E-F, and update affiliations and acknowledgements. An added cross-reference is incorrect: Section 5.6 points to Table 7 rather than the confounding plot in Figure 7.

P2.justification: v2 adds the latent-confounding plot and five numbered tables covering cycles, prior errors, AID, uncertainty and observational results, plus complexity-analysis displays. Figure 2 swaps displayed row/column attention labels, and captions and placements change. The original pooling table and sample-size plot are retained as Table 3 and Figure 8.

improvement.justification: v1's central large-graph claim lacked uncertainty estimates and direct cyclicity checks at that scale. v2 adds these, AID evaluations and targeted robustness tests, substantially improving scrutiny of when discovery succeeds or fails. Expanded efficiency derivations and explicit limits on real-world applicability improve transparency. Unexplained SERGIO-GRN score revisions and inconsistencies involving Tables 1 and 6 and the retained sample-size plot remain, but the diagnostic and reporting gains outweigh these limitations.
